Open Start and type your company name and your numbers in the yellow cells: the tax rates your adviser gives you, years to depreciate, building share, selling cost share, highest LTV (loan divided by value) and wanted return on equity.
Keep Properties up to date: price, closing costs, rehab, value now, exit plan and planned exit year. Total cost, cost basis, loan balance, equity, LTV and the cash from a sale fill in.

Each quarter add a row on Net worth by quarter with the property value, the loan balances and the cash. Net worth (what you own minus what you owe), the change and the target check fill in. Set the targets on Growth targets.
Record every new value on Valuations and Agent opinions of value. An old opinion turns amber so you ask the agent for a new one.

Enter every improvement, fee or insurance payout on Basis adjustments. Depreciation schedule shows the yearly depreciation, the amount taken and what remains. Check the years and the building share with your own adviser.
Read Equity by property and Hold against sell: equity, LTV, room to borrow, return on equity and a signal that shows which property to keep, refinance or review for a sale.

Before you sell, add an Exit analysis for the sale, refinance and exchange options and a Sale plan with the list date, the price and the lowest price. The net cash after the loan payoff, the selling costs and the estimated tax fills in.
If you plan an exchange, add a row on Exchange timeline. The dates come from the day counts in Settings: use the ones your own adviser gives you.
Use Tax set-asides, Tax summary by year and Depreciation to prepare the yearly package, and log every question for your accountant on Adviser questions.

Use the 14 calculators: net worth, equity, cost basis, depreciation, estimated gain, net proceeds, hold or refinance or sell, exchange dates, return on equity, IRR, growth needed, sale against refinance, exit ladder and a grid.
All tax figures are estimates, not tax advice: check with your own adviser and check your own local rules before you act on them.

Cash: what came in and went out each month
One row for each month with the opening and closing cash and every kind of money in and out; cash in, cash out, net change, cash flow before rehab and purchases, and the 12-month totals fill in.
Cash flow before rehab and purchases
13-week forecast: closing cash week by week
One row for each of the next 13 weeks: expected rent and the money going out. Closing cash, headroom and a floor warning fill in. Big payments go in Purchases, balloon, set-aside.
Reserves by property: months of loan payments and costs held
One row for each held property with the reserve you hold; the loan payment, the monthly need, the reserve you should hold, the months covered and the shortfall fill in.
Owner draws: what was taken out and who approved it
One row for each draw with the month, the amount, the reason and who approved it; the total for the month, the total drawn this year, the safe draw today and a check fill in.
Drawn this year to the month
Planned purchases: the cash each deal needs
One row for each purchase you plan: price, down payment, closing costs, rehab and reserve. Cash needed, cash-on-cash return and whether funding is in place fill in.
Funding sources: where the money for purchases can come from
One row for each source of cash with the amount, the cost and the date it is available; the days to wait and a check fill in. Cash on hand is already counted in your cash balance.
Growth targets: doors, cash flow and net worth each quarter
One row for each quarter: doors, monthly net cash flow and net worth, target and actual. Gaps, the share reached and a check fill in. Net worth matches the Net Worth workbook.
Growth scenarios: doors, cash flow and net worth in 5 years
One row for each way to grow with the purchases a year, the price, the cash-on-cash return and the value growth; the doors, the monthly cash flow and the net worth in 5 years fill in from today.
Cash flow a month in 5 years
Rent payments: what each tenant paid and when
One row for each monthly rent payment with the amount due and paid; the unpaid part fills in. Rent collected in the last 30 days reads from here.
Expenses: what was paid for each category, week by week
One row for each cost category and week with the amount paid. Costs paid in the last 30 days read from here.
Loan payments: what each loan cost each month
One row for each loan payment with the payment date, the interest and the amount; the part that repays the loan fills in.
Draws: money released to contractors as work is finished
One row for each contractor draw (a payment released as work is finished) with the request and payment dates; whether it is still open and the days waiting fill in.
Properties: value, strategy and the loan against each
The 16 properties with value, strategy and units; the loan balance and the equity fill in. Values match the Net Worth workbook of this suite.
One row for each loan; the payment, the balance today, the days to a balloon (a loan whose remaining balance is due on one date), the cash on hand and the reserves fill in.
One row for each past sale with the price, the selling costs and the profit; the cash from the sale fills in. The same sales as the Net Worth workbook of this suite.
Upcoming payments: what is due in the next weeks
One row for each payment due or just paid with the kind, the payee and the amount; the days to wait, whether it is open and a due-soon or overdue check fill in. Only open payments can be late.
Cash buffer by month: how many months the cash would last
One row for each month; the cash, the monthly outflow, the months of cost and loan cover and the gap to your cash floor fill in from the Cash page.
Capital calls: money asked from partners and private lenders
One row for each call for money with the partner, the amount and the purpose; whether it is received, the days waiting and a check fill in. Only open calls can be late.
Weekly cash log: cash in, cash out and closing cash
One row for each week with the cash in, the cash out and the closing cash from your bank; the net change, the gap to the floor and a check fill in.

Log every call for money on Capital calls. Set quarterly targets on Growth targets and compare scenarios on Growth scenarios.
